# OneGrid deployment parameter reference

Part of the [OneGrid landing zone design guide](../../architecture/design-guide.md).

[Deploy OneGrid](../README.md) | [Deploy from the command line](../deploy-cli.md) | [Parameter files](../../../planetary-computer-pro-poc/deploy/azure/parameters/README.md)

The OneGrid template, [`main.bicep`](../../../planetary-computer-pro-poc/deploy/azure/main.bicep), declares 45 parameters. The compiled [`azuredeploy.json`](../../../planetary-computer-pro-poc/deploy/azure/azuredeploy.json) declares the same set. This page is generated from the template and the [portal form](../../../planetary-computer-pro-poc/deploy/azure/createUiDefinition.json), so it always matches the code.

- **35** parameters are set by the portal form; **10** are available only from the command line or a parameter file.
- No parameter is required: every parameter has a default. A deployment with no parameters creates only GeoCatalog, sample storage, and the Microsoft Foundry model, because those are the only components whose switches default to `true`.
- The **Template description** column reproduces each parameter's `@description` text verbatim, including the template's own product names. A **Note** adds context where the code behaves differently from the description.
- **Form default** is what the portal form sends when you accept every default on every step. A command-line deployment uses the **Default** column instead, so set component switches explicitly; see [Portal defaults that differ from the template](#portal-defaults-that-differ-from-the-template).

## Region and components

Choose the region and the components to deploy. The web app needs the Fabric plane, the Fabric plane needs sample storage, and the forecast job needs the Aurora model and sample storage; the template skips a component whose dependency is off.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Portal form | Template description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="param-location"></a>`location` | string | `westeurope` | **Basics** › Region. | Azure region for all resources. Planetary Computer Pro GeoCatalog is available only in the regions listed here (Preview). **Allowed:** `eastus`, `northcentralus`, `westeurope`, `canadacentral`, `uksouth`. **Note:** The allowed list applies even when `deployGeoCatalog` is `false`. |
| <a id="param-deploygeocatalog"></a>`deployGeoCatalog` | bool | `true` | **Components** › Components to deploy: *Planetary Computer Pro GeoCatalog*. Form default: `true`. | Deploy the Planetary Computer Pro GeoCatalog (geospatial imagery catalog used by the web app's map layers and asset uploads). Turn off to deploy OneGrid without it; the web app then reads live Fabric data without catalog imagery. |
| <a id="param-deploysamplestorage"></a>`deploySampleStorage` | bool | `true` | **Components** › Components to deploy: *Sample storage + ingestion identity*. Form default: `true`. | Deploy a sample-data storage account and a user-assigned managed identity for the managed-identity ingestion path (bring-your-own-data scenario). |
| <a id="param-deployaiagent"></a>`deployAiAgent` | bool | `true` | **Components** › Components to deploy: *AI agent (Azure OpenAI / Foundry)*. Form default: `true`. | Deploy an Azure OpenAI (Microsoft Foundry) account + model deployment for agentic / reasoning GeoAI scenarios against the GeoCatalog. |
| <a id="param-deployauroramodel"></a>`deployAuroraModel` | bool | `false` | **Components** › Components to deploy: *Aurora weather model (GPU Foundry endpoint)*. Form default: `false`. | Deploy the Microsoft Aurora weather foundation model on a GPU-backed Foundry managed-compute endpoint. Requires GPU (A100) quota, an Azure Marketplace subscription, and acceptance of the model terms. |
| <a id="param-deployauroraschedule"></a>`deployAuroraSchedule` | bool | `false` | **Components** › Components to deploy: *Aurora scheduled forecast job (Container Apps)*. Form default: `false`. | Deploy a scheduled Azure Container Apps Job that runs the Aurora forecast pipeline on the ECMWF cycle cadence (00/06/12/18 UTC), publishing weather-events.json to the model-outputs container so the map stays live without manual runs. The template also provisions a dedicated Azure Container Registry for the pipeline image. Requires the Aurora weather model (for the GPU endpoint) and sample storage. **Note:** The template builds the pipeline image into its own registry (`pcpro-aurora-image-build`), so no prebuilt image is needed unless you set `auroraJobImage`. |
| <a id="param-deployfabricplane"></a>`deployFabricPlane` | bool | `false` | **Components** › Components to deploy: *OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)*. Form default: `true`. | Enable the OneGrid Fabric plane on top of this PCP backend: it provisions a Fabric workspace, lakehouse, eventhouse/KQL database, the geo_point_in_polygon hazard join + composite-risk tables, and (when a connection id is supplied) a OneLake shortcut to the model-outputs container. Fabric is not an ARM resource type, so this runs as an in-template deploymentScript (Fabric REST) using the Fabric-plane identity. Requires deploySampleStorage and an existing Microsoft Fabric capacity. **Note:** An existing capacity isn't required: set `createFabricCapacity` to `true` to have the template create one. |
| <a id="param-deployonegridapp"></a>`deployOneGridApp` | bool | `false` | **Components** › Components to deploy: *OneGrid web app (AI Foundry + chat/report)*. Form default: `true`. | Also stand up the OneGrid web application: the AI Foundry account (reused from the AI agent above when present) and the chat/report Container App, deployed into THIS resource group. Requires the OneGrid Fabric plane. The in-template provisioner runs OneGrid deploy.ps1 for the foundry/dataagent/chatagent phases; because this creates resources and role assignments, the Fabric-plane identity is granted Owner on this resource group. **Note:** The template deploys the web app on App Service (`chatAgentSite`), not Container Apps; see [known issues](../known-issues.md#portal-and-template-text-describe-a-container-app). |
| <a id="param-deployonegriddata"></a>`deployOneGridData` | bool | `false` | **Components** › Components to deploy: *OneGrid historical data seed (large)*. Form default: `true`. | Seed the full OneGrid historical demo dataset into the lakehouse/eventhouse (cloud-seeded from the public release bundle, ~hundreds of MB). Off by default to keep the deployment fast; enable for a fully populated demo. **Note:** The portal form preselects this component although the template default is `false`. |

## Storage policy exemption

Use only when Azure Policy disables shared-key or public network access on new storage accounts and your organization approves the exemption.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Portal form | Template description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="param-exemptstoragefrompolicy"></a>`exemptStorageFromPolicy` | bool | `false` | **Components** › Exempt this deployment's storage from storage policies. Form default: `false`. | Exempt this deployment's storage accounts from Azure Policy that disables shared-key or public network access on storage (for example the Microsoft MCAPS governance policies). When true, the storage accounts are tagged with the opt-out tag below, the deployment scripts run on a dedicated tagged storage account, and public network access is set explicitly. Leave false unless your subscription enforces such a policy and your organization allows the exemption. |
| <a id="param-storagepolicyexemptiontagname"></a>`storagePolicyExemptionTagName` | string | `SecurityControl` | **Components** › Policy exemption tag name. Form default: `SecurityControl`. Sent when *Exempt this deployment's storage from storage policies* is checked; otherwise `SecurityControl`. | Tag name your storage policy honors as an exemption. Used only when exemptStorageFromPolicy is true. |
| <a id="param-storagepolicyexemptiontagvalue"></a>`storagePolicyExemptionTagValue` | string | `Ignore` | **Components** › Policy exemption tag value. Form default: `Ignore`. Sent when *Exempt this deployment's storage from storage policies* is checked; otherwise `Ignore`. | Tag value your storage policy honors as an exemption. Used only when exemptStorageFromPolicy is true. |

## Aurora weather model

The Azure Machine Learning workspace, managed online endpoint, and optional GPU deployment for Aurora. Used only when `deployAuroraModel` is `true`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Portal form | Template description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="param-aurorainstancetype"></a>`auroraInstanceType` | string | `Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4` | **AI** › Aurora weather model (GPU) › GPU instance type. Form default: `Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4`. Sent when *Aurora weather model (GPU Foundry endpoint)* is selected; otherwise `Standard_NC24ads_A100_v4`. | GPU VM size for the Aurora managed-compute deployment. Aurora requires an A100-class SKU; you must have quota for it in the selected region. |
| <a id="param-createauroramodeldeployment"></a>`createAuroraModelDeployment` | bool | `false` | **AI** › Aurora weather model (GPU) › Deploy the Aurora model for me (official published asset). Form default: `false`. Sent when *Aurora weather model (GPU Foundry endpoint)* is selected; otherwise `false`. | Deploy the Aurora model onto the GPU endpoint for me using the official published model asset (azureml://registries/azureml/models/Aurora/versions/4) instead of pasting a model asset ID. Ignored when auroraModelAssetId is supplied. Still requires A100 quota in the region and accepted Azure Marketplace terms for Aurora. |
| <a id="param-auroramodelassetid"></a>`auroraModelAssetId` | string | *(empty)* | **AI** › Aurora weather model (GPU) › Aurora model asset ID (optional). Form default: *(empty)*. Sent when *Aurora weather model (GPU Foundry endpoint)* is selected and *Deploy the Aurora model for me (official published asset)* is cleared; otherwise *(empty)*. | Registry model asset ID for the Aurora managed-compute deployment. The official Microsoft storm-impact app uses azureml://registries/azureml/models/Aurora/versions/4. Leave blank to provision the Foundry workspace + endpoint only and deploy the model from the portal (the GPU deployment needs quota + accepted terms). |

## Forecast job

The scheduled Azure Container Apps job that runs the Aurora pipeline. Used only when `deployAuroraSchedule`, `deployAuroraModel`, and `deploySampleStorage` are all `true`.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Portal form | Template description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="param-aurorajobimage"></a>`auroraJobImage` | string | *(empty)* | **AI** › Aurora scheduled forecast job (Container Apps) › Custom pipeline image (optional override). Form default: *(empty)*. Sent when *Aurora scheduled forecast job (Container Apps)* is selected; otherwise *(empty)*. | Optional override for the Aurora pipeline container image, e.g. myregistry.azurecr.io/aurora-pipeline:latest. Leave blank to use the Azure Container Registry this template provisions (build into it once with `az acr build`). **Note:** When this is blank, the deployment builds the image into the provisioned registry for you; run `az acr build` only to rebuild it. |
| <a id="param-aurorajobimagetag"></a>`auroraJobImageTag` | string | `latest` | Not on the form; the template default applies. | Image tag for the Aurora pipeline image in the auto-provisioned registry. Ignored when auroraJobImage is set. |
| <a id="param-aurorajobcron"></a>`auroraJobCron` | string | `0 1,7,13,19 * * *` | **AI** › Aurora scheduled forecast job (Container Apps) › Schedule (cron, UTC). Form default: `0 1,7,13,19 * * *`. Sent when *Aurora scheduled forecast job (Container Apps)* is selected; otherwise `0 1,7,13,19 * * *`. | Cron schedule (UTC) for the Aurora forecast job. The default runs ~1 h after each synoptic cycle (00/06/12/18 UTC) to allow for input-data latency. |

## Microsoft Fabric

The Fabric capacity, workspace, storage connection, and unified asset model that the Fabric-plane deployment script provisions. Used only when the Fabric plane is deployed.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Portal form | Template description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="param-createfabriccapacity"></a>`createFabricCapacity` | bool | `false` | **Fabric plane** › Create a new Fabric capacity for me. Form default: `false`. Sent when *OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)* is selected; otherwise `false`. | Create a new Microsoft Fabric capacity (F-SKU) in this resource group instead of reusing an existing one. When true, fabricCapacityId is ignored and the Fabric plane deploys onto the freshly created capacity. Note: an F-SKU is billed hourly until paused or deleted; ARM cannot create a free Trial capacity. |
| <a id="param-fabriccapacitysku"></a>`fabricCapacitySku` | string | `F2` | **Fabric plane** › New Fabric capacity SKU. Form default: `F2`. Sent when *OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)* is selected and *Create a new Fabric capacity for me* is checked; otherwise `F2`. | SKU for the auto-created Fabric capacity (used only when createFabricCapacity is true). F2 is the smallest; scale up for heavier workloads. **Allowed:** `F2`, `F4`, `F8`, `F16`, `F32`, `F64`, `F128`, `F256`, `F512`, `F1024`, `F2048`. **Note:** The portal form offers `F2` to `F256`; set larger SKUs from the command line. |
| <a id="param-fabriccapacityadmin"></a>`fabricCapacityAdmin` | string | *(empty)* | **Fabric plane** › Capacity admin (email or object id, optional). Form default: *(empty)*. Sent when *OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)* is selected and *Create a new Fabric capacity for me* is checked; otherwise *(empty)*. | Additional Fabric capacity administrator (used only when createFabricCapacity is true): a user principal name (email) or an Entra object id. The in-template Fabric-plane identity is always added as an admin so provisioning can assign the workspace; add a human admin here so you can manage the capacity in the Fabric portal. |
| <a id="param-fabriccapacityid"></a>`fabricCapacityId` | string | *(empty)* | **Fabric plane** › Existing Fabric capacity (resource ID or GUID). Form default: *(empty)*. Sent when *OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)* is selected and *Create a new Fabric capacity for me* is cleared; otherwise *(empty)*. | Existing Microsoft Fabric capacity resource id or capacity GUID (F-SKU or Trial). Provide one to reuse an existing capacity. Ignored when createFabricCapacity is true (the template provisions a new one instead). |
| <a id="param-fabricworkspacename"></a>`fabricWorkspaceName` | string | `OneGrid` | **Fabric plane** › Fabric workspace name. Form default: `OneGrid`. Sent when *OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)* is selected; otherwise `OneGrid`. | Display name of the Fabric workspace the OneGrid plane provisions. |
| <a id="param-createfabricconnection"></a>`createFabricConnection` | bool | `false` | **Fabric plane** › Create the storage connection for me (workspace identity). Form default: `true`. Sent when *OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)* is selected; otherwise `false`. | Instead of pasting an existing Fabric connection id, have the in-template provisioner create the storage connection for you using the Fabric workspace identity (secret-free): it provisions a workspace identity, grants it Storage Blob Data Reader on the sample storage account, creates an ADLS Gen2 connection bound to that identity, and builds the OneLake shortcut. Ignored when fabricConnectionId is supplied. Requires the Fabric tenant setting for service principals/workspace identities. **Note:** The portal form checks this box by default; the template default is `false`. |
| <a id="param-fabricconnectionid"></a>`fabricConnectionId` | string | *(empty)* | **Fabric plane** › Fabric storage connection ID (optional). Form default: *(empty)*. Sent when *OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)* is selected and *Create the storage connection for me (workspace identity)* is cleared; otherwise *(empty)*. | GUID of a Fabric cloud connection to the sample storage account. Needed only for the OneLake shortcut to the model-outputs container; leave blank to provision the Fabric plane (workspace, lakehouse, eventhouse, hazard KQL) and add the shortcut later. |
| <a id="param-deployunifiedmodel"></a>`deployUnifiedModel` | bool | `true` | **Fabric plane** › Build the unified asset model (recommended). Form default: `true`. Sent when *OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)* is selected and *OneGrid web app (AI Foundry + chat/report)* is selected; otherwise `false`. | Unify Weather + Digital Twin onto one asset spine: the provisioner's 'unified' phase generates the conformed og.* tables (dims + reliability + weather facts) in this deployment's lakehouse and deploys the OneGridModelImport Import model over them, then targets the app (PBI_DATASET) at it. Requires the OneGrid Fabric plane + app, and a refresh identity (grantProvisionerGraphPermission or refreshServicePrincipal*) so the model can be refreshed. On by default. |

## Web app

The App Service plan, the enabled app modules, and the application package. Used only when the web app is deployed.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Portal form | Template description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="param-chatagentappservicesku"></a>`chatAgentAppServiceSku` | string | `B1` | **Fabric plane** › OneGrid web app plan (App Service SKU). Form default: `B1`. Sent when *OneGrid web app (AI Foundry + chat/report)* is selected; otherwise `B1`. | App Service plan pricing tier for the OneGrid chat/report web app. B1 (Basic) is the low-cost default; pick a Premium v3 tier (P0v3/P1v3/P2v3/P3v3) for production-grade CPU/memory, autoscale, and better cold-start. Only applies when the OneGrid web app is deployed. **Allowed:** `B1`, `B2`, `B3`, `S1`, `S2`, `S3`, `P0v3`, `P1v3`, `P2v3`, `P3v3`. |
| <a id="param-onegridmodules"></a>`oneGridModules` | array | `["exec", "weather", "twin", "infra", "sap", "esu", "onerig", "copilot"]` | **App modules** › App modules to enable. Form default: `["exec", "weather", "twin", "infra", "sap", "esu", "onerig", "copilot"]`. | OneGrid app modules to enable in the web app (written to the ONEGRID_MODULES app setting). Allowed ids: exec (Executive Brief), weather (Weather Intelligence), twin (Digital Twin and Simulation), infra (IT/OT Infrastructure), sap (SAP S/4HANA), esu (ESU Planner), onerig (Oil and Gas solution), copilot (Copilot chat). Core pages are always on. An empty list enables only the core pages. |
| <a id="param-onegridapppackageurl"></a>`oneGridAppPackageUrl` | string | `https://github.com/paulshaheen/OneGrid/releases/download/app-latest/onegrid-app.zip` | Not on the form; the template default applies. | SOURCE URL of the prebuilt, self-contained OneGrid web app package (zip) published by the "Release OneGrid App" GitHub Actions workflow. The provisioner downloads this and re-hosts it in the deployment's own (private) storage account; the web app then mounts it read-only via WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE using its managed identity (no public exposure, no SAS). No server-side build runs; the package already contains the built webapp + node_modules. **Note:** The default points at the mutable `app-latest` release. Pin a versioned package for production. |

## Identity and sign-in

Microsoft Entra sign-in for the web app and the identity that binds and refreshes the Import semantic model.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Portal form | Template description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="param-enableentrasignin"></a>`enableEntraSignIn` | bool | `true` | **Components** › Components to deploy: *OneGrid web app (AI Foundry + chat/report)*. Form default: `true`. | Enable automatic Entra ID sign-in wiring for the Explorer web app. When true, the provisioner creates (or reuses) a SPA app registration and sets ENTRA_CLIENT_ID/ENTRA_TENANT_ID. Auto-create requires the deployment identity to hold Microsoft Graph Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy; otherwise supply entraSignInClientId. **Note:** The portal form sends `true` whenever the web app is selected. Set `false` from the command line to skip sign-in wiring. |
| <a id="param-entrasigninclientid"></a>`entraSignInClientId` | string | *(empty)* | **Fabric plane** › Existing sign-in app registration (client ID). Form default: *(empty)*. Sent when *OneGrid web app (AI Foundry + chat/report)* is selected and *Create the sign-in (Entra SPA) app registration for me* is cleared; otherwise *(empty)*. | Optional pre-created Entra ID (SPA) app registration client ID for sign-in. Supply this when the deployment identity cannot create app registrations. Its SPA redirect URI must include https://&lt;app-host&gt;/auth/callback. **Note:** The provisioner doesn't add the redirect URI to a pre-created registration; add `https://<app-host>/auth/callback` yourself. |
| <a id="param-grantprovisionergraphpermission"></a>`grantProvisionerGraphPermission` | bool | `false` | **Fabric plane** › Grant the deployment identity permission to create app registrations. Form default: `false`. Sent when *OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)* is selected; otherwise `false`. | Grant the deployment identity (pcpro-fabricplane-identity) the Microsoft Graph application permission Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy, so the setup scripts can create the Entra sign-in app registration and the service principal that binds and refreshes the Import semantic model. The person deploying must be able to grant Graph application permissions (Privileged Role Administrator or Global Administrator). Without it, sign-in stays unconfigured and the Import model is not refreshed. |
| <a id="param-refreshserviceprincipalclientid"></a>`refreshServicePrincipalClientId` | string | *(empty)* | **Fabric plane** › Refresh service principal client ID (optional). Form default: *(empty)*. Sent when *OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)* is selected and *Grant the deployment identity permission to create app registrations* is cleared; otherwise *(empty)*. | Optional existing service principal (app registration) the setup scripts use to bind and refresh the Import semantic model, when the deployment identity cannot create one (grantProvisionerGraphPermission off). Client (application) ID. |
| <a id="param-refreshserviceprincipalobjectid"></a>`refreshServicePrincipalObjectId` | string | *(empty)* | **Fabric plane** › Refresh service principal object ID. Form default: *(empty)*. Sent when *OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)* is selected and *Grant the deployment identity permission to create app registrations* is cleared and *Refresh service principal client ID (optional)* has a value; otherwise *(empty)*. | Object ID of the service principal (enterprise application) for refreshServicePrincipalClientId. |
| <a id="param-refreshserviceprincipalsecret"></a>`refreshServicePrincipalSecret` | string (secure) | *(empty)* | **Fabric plane** › Refresh service principal client secret. Form default: *(empty)*. Sent when *OneGrid Fabric plane (OneLake + hazard join)* is selected and *Grant the deployment identity permission to create app registrations* is cleared and *Refresh service principal client ID (optional)* has a value; otherwise *(empty)*. | Client secret for refreshServicePrincipalClientId. **Note:** Pass it from Azure Key Vault (a parameter-file reference or `az.getSecret()`), never as plain text. |

## Source and internal

Where the deployment scripts get the provisioner, and the internal per-deployment seed. Pin the source for production environments.

| Parameter | Type | Default | Portal form | Template description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="param-onegridrepourl"></a>`oneGridRepoUrl` | string | `https://github.com/paulshaheen/OneGrid.git` | Not on the form; the template default applies. | Git repository the in-template provisioner clones OneGrid deploy.ps1 + accelerator content from. The OneGrid monorepo keeps the orchestrator at planetary-computer-pro-poc/infra/deploy.ps1. |
| <a id="param-onegridref"></a>`oneGridRef` | string | `main` | Not on the form; the template default applies. | Git ref (branch/tag/commit) of the OneGrid repository to deploy. **Note:** The scripts clone with `git clone --depth 1 --branch`, which accepts a branch or tag but not a commit SHA. Pin a tag for production. |
| <a id="param-deploymenttoken"></a>`deploymentToken` | string | `utcNow()` (expression) | Not on the form; the template default applies. | Internal: unique per-deployment seed (do not set manually). Used ONLY to keep the Aurora Key Vault name fresh on every deployment operation, because Key Vault soft-deletes for 90 days and a name derived only from the resource group id collides with a vault left over from an earlier failed/torn-down deployment into the same RG (ConflictError: "A vault with the same name already exists in deleted state"). **Note:** Don't set it. Every deployment gets a new Aurora Key Vault name and re-runs the deployment scripts because of it. |

## Portal defaults that differ from the template

When you accept every default, the portal form sends these values, which differ from the template defaults. Set them explicitly in a command-line deployment to get the same result as the portal; the [`baseline-required`](../../../planetary-computer-pro-poc/deploy/azure/parameters/README.md) parameter file does.

| Parameter | Template default | Portal form default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`deployFabricPlane`](#param-deployfabricplane) | `false` | `true` |
| [`createFabricConnection`](#param-createfabricconnection) | `false` | `true` |
| [`deployOneGridApp`](#param-deployonegridapp) | `false` | `true` |
| [`deployOneGridData`](#param-deployonegriddata) | `false` | `true` |

The form's region has no fixed default: you choose it on the **Basics** step from the allowed list. The template default is `westeurope`.

With every default kept, the form also requires these values before **Review + create** succeeds, because their controls are shown, required, and blank:

- [`fabricCapacityId`](#param-fabriccapacityid): **Fabric plane** › Existing Fabric capacity (resource ID or GUID).

## Regenerate this page

Run the generator after you change `main.bicep` or `createUiDefinition.json`, and commit the result with the template change:

```powershell
python docs/deploy/build_reference.py
python -m unittest discover -s docs/deploy -p "test_*.py"
```

`python docs/deploy/build_reference.py --check` exits with an error when this page is stale. The tests also check that every parameter is documented and that the shipped parameter files use only real parameter names.
